text:
zoe.design: dropping a quick pass on the threshold preview density. In the new layout the preview sits below the fold on 13" laptops when there are 3+ thresholds. Frame: https://img.redwood.local/frames/threshold_density_v1.png
matt.pm: good catch. Product ask: preview needs to be visible without scrolling for one-screen health checks. Can we collapse non-essential chrome (long breadcrumbs & help links) to reclaim vertical space?
kai.eng: technically straightforward: we can collapse breadcrumbs into a single compact crumb with a chevron menu, and hide the long help link behind a kebab. That should free ~72px.
leah.sre: accessibility / UX question: if we tuck things away, make sure the visual order equals DOM order for screen readers. Also don't hide keyboard-only affordances.
nina.content: copy thought: users often misread "Suppress" vs "Mute". Research feedback shows "Quiet window" was clearer for non-SRE folks. @omar.research had some interview notes.
omar.research: true — in 5 interviews folks used "mute" or "quiet" in their language. Suggest testing label alternatives: "Suppress (quiet window)" or just "Quiet window" with tooltip "Silences notifications for X time".
zoe.design: notation: if we rename, we need to adjust tooltip language and the preview banner copy to match. Proposed banner: "Quiet window on 1 muted for 2 hours; routes unchanged." Keep <= 100 chars.
matt.pm: thumbs up to testing labels. Also product asks that the preview banner include an inline "Undo" action for quick reversal. Must be keyboard accessible.
kai.eng: implementable: banner will expose a small button "Undo" with aria-label="Undo quiet window" and will be focusable. We'll add a shortcut: pressing U while banner focused triggers the undo.
leah.sre: keyboard flow: tab order must go: threshold rows -> preview pills -> banner -> actions. Right now banner gets rendered after actions and tab skips it. DOM reorder needed.
a11ybot: accessibility reminder: use role="status" + aria-live="polite" for the preview banner. Do NOT use assertive. Debounce announcements by 250-400ms to avoid spam when users are typing.
zoe.design: visual distinction: suggestion is to make route pill filled with icon (arrow), quiet window pill outlined with small speaker-off icon. For color-blind users include an extra shape or stripe.
omar.research: interview data: people notice icons faster than subtle color shifts. Icons + text will help. Also call out that "Route" implies action; maybe label it "Route to" to clarify it's an action that chooses a destination.
nina.content: microcopy proposals: pill labels: "Route to" / "Quiet window". Tooltip for route: "Routes alert to selected channel(s)" Tooltip for quiet: "Silences alerts for selected duration". Empty state: "No alert thresholds yet — create one to start getting notified." CTA: "Create threshold".
kai.eng: implementation note: we'll export a merged-preview object from the backend: { preview_id: string, preview_text: string, preview_html_safe: boolean, preview_state: "merged" }. Frontend should update innerText of the stable container (id=preview-<preview_id>) to avoid replacing the node. That preserves focus and screen reader context.
leah.sre: please ensure the banner container keeps the same id across updates. Tests should assert focus is not lost when preview_text changes.
a11ybot: keyboard checklist: roving tabindex for pill group, each pill has role="button" and tabindex managed, chevron has aria-expanded toggled, Undo button has accessible name, and reduced-motion respected for expand/collapse.
zoe.design: motion note: use a 120ms fade for the preview text change and respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce to no animation.
matt.pm: mobile constraints: on small screens the preview should be pinned above the primary CTA row. If necessary, shorten pill labels and show full text in tooltip/expanded view.
omar.research: quick usability test plan: 6 participants, task: set a threshold and enable quiet window. Measure if they notice preview banner and can undo it via keyboard within 30s. We'll run this next week.
nina.content: one more copy nit: banner wording options: "Quiet window on — alerts silenced for 2 hours" vs "Quiet window enabled — alerts silenced for 2 hours". Shorter is usually better for quick scans.
a11ybot: color contrast check: ensure outlined quiet pill stroke achieves >=3:1 against background in both light/dark themes. Add non-color affordance (icon or stripe).
kai.eng: I'll prototype the compact crumb + DOM reorder and draft the preview_id contract. Will add a 300ms debounce on frontend and server-side throttle to keep updates reasonable.
zoe.design: thanks team. I'll update the Figma frames with compact breadcrumb, outlined quiet pill with icon, banner with Undo, and reduced-motion variants. Tagging @kai.eng @leah.sre @omar.research for follow-ups.
matt.pm: adding product acceptance: preview visible without vertical scroll on 13" laptop with up to 3 thresholds, Undo present and keyboardable, merged-preview id stable, and labels A/B tested.
a11ybot: recorded: actions -> compact breadcrumb, DOM reorder to place banner before actions, outlined quiet pill + icon, role=status + aria-live=polite + 300ms debounce, preview_id stability, Undo button with accessible name, roving tabindex, reduced-motion support, contrast >=3:1.
zoe.design: will post updated frames by EOD and schedule a short sync if needed. Thanks all!
